description:
ContactCard keeps all 22 RFC 9553 sub-object fields as Option<serde_json::Value> on the wire, then re-exports jmap-jscontact-types::* at the top level (and as the 'jscontact' module alias) so callers can opt into typed deserialization via serde_json::from_value. This is the right shape for a draft-evolving spec where the wire-format object owns the schema:

- Round-trip fidelity: any new RFC 9553 sub-object field added in a future RFC revision deserializes losslessly without code changes here.
- Forward-compat: vendors who extend a sub-object value (within the spec's permitted extension points) round-trip cleanly.
- Opt-in typing: callers who want compile-time typed access get it via jmap_contacts_types::Name (or ::jscontact::Name).
- Decoupled release cadence: jmap-jscontact-types can update its typed sub-types without forcing a contacts-types breaking change.

A future contributor will be tempted to 'simplify' by promoting these 22 fields to concrete typed structs. Do not accept that simplification without a workspace-architectural bead — the hybrid is the deliberate workspace pattern, also used by jmap-calendars-types/jscalendar.
title: GOOD: hybrid sloppy-Value + opt-in typed sub-types via jscontact re-exports
